mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when CPI YoY growth exceeds 3%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of the instances when RSAFS declines for three consecutive months, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a robust supply-side expansion, which is typically associated with a strong economy and positive corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 2% MoM, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy in the face of inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is above 5% and CPIAUCSL YoY growth is above 2%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 jobs in a month signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when PAYEMS decreases by more than 100,000, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals a strengthening demand environment, which is typically associated with a strong economy and positive corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 10% MoM, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an easing monetary cycle, which typically leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 45% of the instances when FEDFUNDS decreases for three consecutive months, this hypothesis is rejected.
